column1: # Real stock-bond DEPENDENCE ASYMMETRY: the exceedance correlations behind the `tail hedge
# corr` fidelity row, which AsymmetryAnchorSuite / asymmetry_anchor_tests re-derive from this
# file. Editing a row moves the shipped anchor. Nothing else is fitted from this file.
# Convention is uni.apps.MarketSim's own (close-only daily log returns, shared dates only):
#   corrFull  corr(r_eq, r_bond) over the window
#   corrL     the same, on sessions with r_eq STRICTLY below its own q10 (index floor(0.10*n)
#             of the ascending sort)
#   corrR     the same, above q90
# WHAT THIS FILE SETTLES. The flight-to-quality hedge HOLDS in the left tail: corrL reads
# -0.24..-0.27 against corrFull -0.26..-0.31 on every pair, where tail-conditioning a bivariate
# normal at that full-sample correlation would decay it toward zero (Longin-Solnik 2001 /
# Ang-Chen 2002, read on the one pair this two-asset model can represent). The asymmetry is
# against that normal baseline, NOT against corrFull: corrL sits 0.03-0.06 above corrFull
# (slightly LESS negative), corrR likewise, so a row built on corrL - corrFull would grade
# noise. corrL itself is the anchor. The window is TLT's own history -- a disinflation era
# throughout, which is why the model-side statistic is measured on its CALM-REGIME sessions
# (the same conditioning `corr_calm` already uses); a century pooling inflation regimes is not
# comparable on any column.
# Measured 2026-08-31, data through 2026-08-20; TLT limits every pair to 2002-07-30..
